full_record.title: Minimal difference set embedding conjecture for abelian difference sets
full_record.statement:
Let $D$ be a normalized difference set with parameters

$$
((q^s+1)(q^{2s}+1),q^{2s}+q^s+1,q^s+1)
$$

in an abelian group $G$. A difference set with parameters $((q+1)(q^2+1),q^2+q+1,q+1)$ is called a **minimal difference set** when $q=p^r$, where $p$ is prime and $r$ is a power of $2$.

**Minimal difference set embedding conjecture.** The difference set $D$ contains a minimal difference set embedded in it: there exists a subgroup $S$ of $G$ such that

$$
D\cap S=D',
$$

where $D'$ is a minimal difference set.

This conjecture proposes a partial generalization of the known embedding results for planar abelian difference sets. The source presents it as still open, while giving only a partial generalization in the preceding theorem.
full_record.source_name: Kevin Jennings, “On Abelian Difference Sets with Parameters of 3-dimensional Projective Geometries”, arXiv:0704.2203 (2007).
full_record.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/0704.2203

Status: no resolution is reported in the source (as of April 2007).

full_record.title: Infinite-mean initial-degree conjecture for the PARID model
full_record.statement: Let $r_k_{k\geq 1}$ be the distribution of the initial degrees in the PARID model, and suppose that it is a power-law distribution with exponent $\tau_{\scriptscriptstyle {\rm W}}\in(1,2)$. **PARID infinite-mean conjecture.** The degree sequence in the PARID model obeys a power law with the same exponent $\tau_{\scriptscriptstyle {\rm W}}$. Since $\tau_{\scriptscriptstyle {\rm W}}\in(1,2)$, the initial-degree distribution has infinite mean; the paper conjectures that its exponent determines the resulting degree sequence in this regime.
full_record.source_name: Maria Deijfen, Henri van den Esker, Remco van der Hofstad and Gerard Hooghiemstra, “A preferential attachment model with random initial degrees”, arXiv:0705.4151 (2020).
full_record.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/0705.4151

Status: no resolution is reported in the source (as of May 2007).

full_record.title: Oriented-cycle conjecture for knot cycle presentations
full_record.statement: Let $K$ be a non-trivial knot and let $D$ be an $n$-cycle presentation of $K$. Let $G(D)$ be the directed graph whose vertices correspond to the edges of $D$, with an oriented edge determined by the over-under relation between two crossing edges. **Oriented-cycle conjecture.** The graph $G(D)$ contains at least one oriented cycle. This conjecture concerns the structure of directed graphs arising from cycle presentations of knots; the supplied text gives no resolution or evidence establishing it.
full_record.source_name: Makoto Ozawa, “Segment number of knots”, arXiv:0705.4348 (2026).
full_record.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/0705.4348

Status: no resolution is reported in the source (as of May 2007).

full_record.title: The subdivision–tropical oriented matroid correspondence
full_record.statement: Let $\Delta_{n-1}$ and $\Delta_{d-1}$ be simplices, and let a tropical oriented matroid have parameters $(n,d)$. A subdivision is a polyhedral subdivision of the product $\Delta_{n-1}\times\Delta_{d-1}$. **The subdivision–tropical oriented matroid correspondence.** There is a one-to-one correspondence between the subdivisions of $\Delta_{n-1}\times\Delta_{d-1}$ and the tropical oriented matroids with parameters $(n,d)$. Realizable tropical oriented matroids are already in canonical bijection with regular subdivisions; the conjecture asserts that this correspondence extends to all subdivisions and tropical oriented matroids, with the elimination axiom as the remaining issue in the stated partial results.
full_record.source_name: Federico Ardila and Mike Develin, “Tropical hyperplane arrangements and oriented matroids”, arXiv:0706.2920 (2007).
full_record.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/0706.2920

Status: no resolution is reported in the source (as of June 2007).

full_record.title: The generic rigidity conjecture for k-triangulations
full_record.statement: A **$k$-triangulation** is a maximal set of pairwise noncrossing diagonals of a convex polygon in which no $k+1$ diagonals mutually cross. A graph is **generically minimally rigid in dimension $d$** if a generic embedding of its vertices in $d$-dimensional Euclidean space is minimally rigid. **Generic rigidity conjecture.** Every $k$-triangulation is generically minimally rigid in dimension $2k$. The conjecture extends the Laman characterization of generic minimal rigidity in the plane; the paper proves it for $k=2$, while the general case remains open.
full_record.source_name: Vincent Pilaud and Francisco Santos, “Multi-triangulations as complexes of star polygons”, arXiv:0706.3121 (2007).
full_record.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/0706.3121

Status: no resolution is reported in the source (as of June 2007).

full_record.title: Nonexistence conjecture for four-dimensional faces of permutation polytopes
full_record.statement:
Let $Q_1$ and $Q_2$ be the four-dimensional polytopes referenced in the classification table of the paper.

**Nonexistence conjecture.** There are no four-dimensional faces of permutation polytopes having the combinatorial type of $Q_1$ or $Q_2$.

These polytopes are exceptional among the classified low-dimensional faces because they do not have the facet-complement property shared by the other examples. The paper reports no resolution of this nonexistence claim.
full_record.source_name: Barbara Baumeister, Christian Haase, Benjamin Nill and Andreas Paffenholz, “On permutation polytopes”, arXiv:0709.1615 (2007).
full_record.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/0709.1615

Status: no resolution is reported in the source (as of September 2007).

full_record.title: Strong embedding conjecture for permutation polytopes
full_record.statement:
Let $P$ be a $d$-dimensional permutation polytope. A permutation polytope is the convex hull of permutation matrices associated with a permutation group, and two polytopes may be combinatorially equivalent or lattice equivalent.

**Strong embedding conjecture.** There exists a permutation group $G\leq S_{2d}$ such that $P(G)$ is combinatorially equivalent, or more strongly lattice equivalent, to $P$.

The bound $2d$ is suggested to be sharp by the example of the $d$-cube, while the paper notes that the existence of some bound follows from an earlier proposition. The claim is presented as open.
full_record.source_name: Barbara Baumeister, Christian Haase, Benjamin Nill and Andreas Paffenholz, “On permutation polytopes”, arXiv:0709.1615 (2007).
full_record.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/0709.1615

Status: no resolution is reported in the source (as of September 2007).

full_record.title: Hirsch equality conjecture for non-degenerate axial transportation polytopes
full_record.statement:
Let $P$ be a non-degenerate $l\times m\times n$ axial transportation polytope with $l,m,n\geq 3$. Its dimension is

$$
d=lmn-l-m-n+2.
$$

Let $f$ be the number of facets of $P$, and let $G(P)$ be its graph. **Hirsch equality conjecture.** The diameter of $G(P)$ is equal to $f-d$. The Hirsch conjecture concerns the general upper bound $f-d$ for the diameter of a $d$-dimensional polytope with $f$ facets; the supplied source does not state a resolution of this stronger equality claim, so it remains open.
full_record.source_name: Jesús A. De Loera, Edward D. Kim, Shmuel Onn and Francisco Santos, “Graphs of Transportation Polytopes”, arXiv:0709.2189 (2009).
full_record.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/0709.2189

Status: no resolution is reported in the source (as of September 2007).

full_record.title: The extremal 3/4 conjecture for fix-free code extension constants
full_record.statement:
Let $P_\gamma$ denote the property that every relevant partial fix-free code whose Kraftsum is at most $\gamma$ can be extended in the manner defined in the survey; let $\gamma^*$ be the supremum of the values of $\gamma$ for which this property holds. **Extremal extension conjecture.**

$$
\sup_{\gamma\ \text{fulfill }}\gamma=\frac{3}{4}.
$$

The survey establishes that some $\gamma\in[\frac12,\frac34]$ satisfies the property and that no $\gamma>\frac34$ does, leaving the exact supremum as the conjectural part.
full_record.source_name: Holger Schnettler, “On the 3/4-Conjecture for Fix-Free Codes – A Survey”, arXiv:0709.2598 (2007).
full_record.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/0709.2598

Status: no resolution is reported in the source (as of September 2007).

full_record.title: Perimeter-preserving bijection for two-staircase unimodal polygons
full_record.statement: Let a unimodal polygon have two staircase regions with identical sides, possibly differing widths, and let the two boxes delimiting the staircase region be identified as in the proposition. Consider the polygons whose bottom perimeter intersects the right box but not the left, and those whose bottom perimeter intersects both boxes. **Perimeter-preserving bijection conjecture.** There exists a perimeter-preserving bijection between these two classes of polygons, where perimeter preserving means that the horizontal and vertical perimeters remain constant. The proposition establishes equality of their generating functions, but the existence of an explicit perimeter-preserving bijection is not established here.
full_record.source_name: W. R. G. James, I. Jensen and A. J. Guttmann, “Families of m-convex polygons: m = 2”, arXiv:0710.4606 (2007).
full_record.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/0710.4606

Status: no resolution is reported in the source (as of October 2007).

full_record.title: The rational-generating-function conjecture below $\kappa$
full_record.statement:
Let $\kappa$ denote the threshold for the small permutation classes studied in the paper, and let a permutation class $\mathcal{C}$ have growth rate $\mathrm{gr}(\mathcal{C})$.

**Rational-generating-function conjecture.** Every permutation class with growth rate less than $\kappa$ has a rational generating function.
Classes of growth rate below $2$ are known to have rational generating functions because they cannot contain arbitrarily long alternations; the conjecture asks whether rationality continues throughout the range below $\kappa$.
full_record.source_name: Vincent Vatter, “Small permutation classes”, arXiv:0712.4006 (2016).
full_record.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/0712.4006

Status: no resolution is reported in the source (as of December 2007).

full_record.title: Kitakubo's planar emulator conjecture
full_record.statement: All graphs considered are finite and simple. A **finite planar emulator** of a graph is a finite emulator whose source graph is planar, and a graph **embeds in the projective plane** when it has a drawing in $\mathbb{R}P^2$ with no edge crossings. **Kitakubo's planar emulator conjecture.** A connected graph has a finite planar emulator if and only if it embeds in the projective plane. Kitakubo proved the corresponding statement for finite planar regular emulators. The general conjecture remains open in the source, although its relation to the unresolved covering question for $K_{1,2,2,2}$ is discussed.
full_record.source_name: Yo'av Rieck and Yasushi Yamashita, “Finite planar emulators for K_4,5 - 4K_2 and K_1,2,2,2 and Fellows' Conjecture”, arXiv:0812.3700 (2009).
full_record.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/0812.3700

Status: **refuted** according to the source (as of December 2008). “D. Archdeacon showed that $K_{4,5} - 4K_2$ does not admit a finite planar cover; thus $K_{4,5} - 4K_2$ provides a counterexample to Fellows' Conjecture.”

full_record.title: The planar graph braid group commutator presentation conjecture
full_record.statement:
Let $\Gamma$ be a planar graph, and let $B_2\Gamma$ denote its braid group on two strands. A presentation for $B_2\Gamma$ should exist in which every relator is a commutator associated to a pair of disjoint simple loops.

**Planar graph braid group commutator presentation conjecture.** There exists a presentation for $B_2\Gamma$ such that the relators are all commutators corresponding to pairs of disjoint simple loops.

This would generalize the preceding theorem, which establishes the analogous presentation result in the setting treated there. The parser supplies no evidence that the conjecture has been resolved.
full_record.source_name: Daniel Farley and Lucas Sabalka, “Presentations of Graph Braid Groups”, arXiv:0907.2730 (2009).
full_record.references:
**2 papers in this index state this conjecture** (2008–2009). The statement above is taken from the most recent of them; the others are [arXiv:0805.0082](https://arxiv.org/abs/0805.0082).

Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/0907.2730

Status: no resolution is reported in the source (as of July 2009).

full_record.title: Bipartite monochromatic path partition conjecture
full_record.statement: Let $K_{n,n}$ be a balanced complete bipartite graph whose edges are coloured with $r$ colours. A **vertex-partition into monochromatic paths** is a partition of all vertices into paths, each having edges of one colour. **Bipartite path partition conjecture.** Suppose that the edges of $K_{n,n}$ are coloured with $r$ colours. There is a vertex-partition of $K_{n,n}$ into $2r-1$ monochromatic paths. This conjecture would generalise the paper's earlier result for balanced complete bipartite graphs and is proposed as a direction beyond complete graphs.
full_record.source_name: Alexey Pokrovskiy, “Partitioning edge-coloured complete graphs into monochromatic cycles and paths”, arXiv:1205.5492 (2012).
full_record.references:
**2 papers in this index state this conjecture** (2007–2012). The statement above is taken from the most recent of them; the others are [arXiv:math/0702354](https://arxiv.org/abs/math/0702354).

Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/1205.5492

Status: **open** according to the source (as of May 2012). “This conjecture is open for $r\geq 3$.”

full_record.title: Inverse conjecture for the large sieve with additively structured sieving sets
full_record.statement:
Let $X$ be positive. For each prime $p<X^{1/2}$, let $\Omega_p\subseteq\mathbb{Z}/p\mathbb{Z}$, and let $A\subseteq[1,X]$ be obtained by sieving out the congruence classes in $\Omega_p$. Here a set $\Omega_p$ is **additively structured** if there is an $a\not\equiv0\pmod p$ such that

$$
\left|\sum_{x\in\Omega_p}e\left(\frac{ax}{p}\right)\right|\gg C_pp,
$$

where $C_p\gg\log^{-1}p$.

**Refined inverse conjecture for the large sieve.** Under these assumptions,

$$
|A|\ll X^\epsilon.
$$

The conjecture predicts that simultaneous additive structure in all the sieving sets forces the sifted set to be very small, refining the usual inverse large-sieve conjecture.
full_record.source_name: Farzad Aryan, “Distribution of squares modulo a composite number”, arXiv:1502.05062 (2015).
full_record.references:
**2 papers in this index state this conjecture** (2008–2015). The statement above is taken from the most recent of them; the others are [arXiv:0807.5037](https://arxiv.org/abs/0807.5037).

Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/1502.05062

Status: no resolution is reported in the source (as of February 2015).

full_record.title: The Schatten norm conjecture for r-partite graphs
full_record.statement:
Let $p>2$, $n\geq r\geq2$, and let $G$ be an $r$-partite graph of order $n$. Let $T_r(n)$ be the Turán graph on $n$ vertices.

**Schatten norm conjecture for r-partite graphs.** If $G$ is an $r$-partite graph of order $n$, then

$$
\|G\|_p<\|T_r(n)\|_p,
$$

unless $G=T_r(n)$.

The analogous assertion is stated as an elementary extremal result for $p=2$. For $p>2$, the paper presents this strict Turán extremality statement as plausible, while the preceding constructions provide lower-bound evidence relevant to the problem.
full_record.source_name: Vladimir Nikiforov, “Beyond graph energy: norms of graphs and matrices”, arXiv:1510.02850 (2016).
full_record.references:
**3 papers in this index state this conjecture** (2007–2015). The statement above is taken from the most recent of them; the others are [arXiv:1201.5232](https://arxiv.org/abs/1201.5232), [arXiv:math/0702186](https://arxiv.org/abs/math/0702186).

Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/1510.02850

Status: no resolution is reported in the source (as of October 2015).

full_record.title: Körner–Malvenuto's maximal colliding-permutations conjecture
full_record.statement:
Let $[n]=\{1,\dots,n\}$. Two permutations $\pi_1,\pi_2$ of $[n]$ are **colliding** if there is an index $i\in[n]$ such that $|\pi_1(i)-\pi_2(i)|=1$.

**Körner–Malvenuto's conjecture.** The maximal number of pairwise colliding permutations of $[n]$ is

$$
\binom{n}{\left\lfloor \frac{n}{2} \right\rfloor}.
$$

The paper recalls this earlier extremal question as motivation for studying graph-different Hamiltonian paths. Its status is not specified in the source.
full_record.source_name: István Kovács and Dániel Soltész, “Triangle-different Hamiltonian paths”, arXiv:1608.05237 (2016).
full_record.references:
**3 papers in this index state this conjecture** (2007–2016). The statement above is taken from the most recent of them; the others are [arXiv:1106.0725](https://arxiv.org/abs/1106.0725), [arXiv:0712.1442](https://arxiv.org/abs/0712.1442).

Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/1608.05237

Status: **open** according to the source (as of August 2016). “The maximal number of $C_4$- or $K_4$-different Hamiltonian paths is also an open question at the time, even the correct order of magnitude is unknown.”

full_record.title: Czabarka's conjecture for partially intersecting partition systems
full_record.statement:
Let $\mathcal{P}^n_k$ be the family of $k$-partitions of an $n$-set. Two partitions are **partially $2$-intersecting** if some class of one and some class of the other have intersection of size at least $2$; a system is partially $2$-intersecting if every pair is so related. Let $S(n-1,k)$ denote the corresponding extremal quantity used in the source.

**Czabarka's conjecture.** If $n\leq2k-1$ and $\mathcal{P}\subseteq\mathcal{P}^n_k$ is a partially $2$-intersecting partition system, then 
$$
|\mathcal{P}|\leq S(n-1,k).
$$
 

The conjecture is attributed in the source to Czabarka and is cited to Erdős and Székely. The bound is attained by the system of partitions having a class containing a fixed pair.
full_record.source_name: Karen Meagher, “Covering arrays on graphs: qualitative independence graphs and extremal set partition theory”, arXiv:math/0701553 (2007).
full_record.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/math/0701553

Status: no resolution is reported in the source (as of January 2007).

full_record.title: Bessis's cyclic sieving conjecture for the modified action on $m$-divisible noncrossing partitions
full_record.statement:
Let $W$ be a well-generated complex reflection group with Coxeter number $h$, let $m\geq 0$, and let $NC^m(W)$ be the set of $m$-divisible noncrossing partitions. Define

$$
\mathrm{Cat}^m(W,q)=\prod_{i=1}^{n}\frac{[mh+d_i]_q}{[d_i]_q}.
$$

Let $C'=\mathbb Z/(m+1)h\mathbb Z$ act on $NC^m(W)$ by the modified cyclic action described in the source.

**Bessis's modified-action CSP conjecture.** The triple

$$
(X,X(q),C')=\left(NC^m(W),\mathrm{Cat}^m(W,q),\mathbb Z/(m+1)h\mathbb Z\right)
$$

exhibits the cyclic sieving phenomenon.

The modified action is related to the action for $NC^{m+1}(W)$ and has an interpretation via the Garside automorphism of the divided category associated with the dual braid monoid. The source gives no resolution status.
full_record.source_name: David Bessis and Victor Reiner, “Cyclic sieving of noncrossing partitions for complex reflection groups”, arXiv:math/0701792 (2009).
full_record.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/math/0701792

Status: no resolution is reported in the source (as of January 2007).

full_record.title: Maximality conjecture for the symmetric group in the quantum permutation group
full_record.statement: Let $\mathcal Q_n$ be the quantum permutation group on $n$ points, containing the classical symmetric group $S_n$. **Maximality conjecture.** The symmetric group $S_n$ is maximal in the quantum permutation group $\mathcal Q_n$, for any $n$. This conjecture concerns the classification of quantum subgroups of $\mathcal Q_n$ and asks whether the classical symmetric group can be enlarged within $\mathcal Q_n$ only trivially. The surrounding discussion indicates that the classification problem is understood as difficult for general $n$ and is expected to be accessible first for small values such as $n=5,6,7$.
full_record.source_name: Teodor Banica and Julien Bichon, “Quantum groups acting on 4 points”, arXiv:math/0703118 (2007).
full_record.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/math/0703118

Status: no resolution is reported in the source (as of March 2007).
